newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND FACE TOUGH CHALLENGE AGAINST PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NEW ZEALAND FACE TOUGH CHALLENGE AGAINST PAKISTAN.

text.p: New Zealand need to improve their performance dramatically if they aim to stop a confident Pakistan in the final of the Singer Champions Trophy cricket tournament on Friday.

The tournament has provided the Kiwis, who are flying straight to Pakistan from here for a test and a one-day series, an ideal warm-up to build a strong combination for the tough battles ahead, New Zealand coach Steve Rixon said.

"Agreed, we have lost both the matches to Pakistan in league stages, but the defeats have certainly hardened the attitude of the players," he said. "They are all charged up to make amends in the final."
But New Zealand suffered a big blow in the run-up to the final when their premier fast bowler Simon Doull was ruled out through a hamstring injury.
"At the moment he is undergoing treatment and is it is highly unlikely that he will be able to bowl tomorrow," Rixon said.
He felt a score of 220 or 230 should be a winning score for the side batting first on this wicket where the ball tends to keep a bit low.
Pakistan manager Mushtaq Mohammed echoed similar feelings. "We need to score at least 230 to be in a safe position," he said, adding that his team needed to work ever harder in fielding.
"We have done well in league stages, but then that's history. New Zealand is a pretty strong team and if their top batsmen get going they can pose a serious threat," he said.
Mushtaq said he was a little concerned about his middle order.
"Though our openers are doing fine, we also need good scores from Salim Malik and Ijaz Ahmed in the middle to releave pressures on the lower order."
The Pakistan team have no injury worries. Skipper Wasim Akram, who skipped the last league match against New Zealand to rest his sore shoulder, is recovering well.

Meanwhile, Sri Lanka have appealed to the International Cricket Conference to "tighten up" the standard playing rules to avoid any confusion. Sri Lanka missed out on the final to New Zealand due to the interpretation of Rule 11.1 when "aggregate outcome of matches between two teams" rather than net run rate decided the finalist.

"We are not filing any official protest in the best interest of the game, but we would certainly like the ICC to be more specific in framing rules," said Dhammika Ranatunga, chief executive of the Sri Lankan cricket board.
